articles.title: Systemic Hypertension and Survival in Pulmonary Hypertension

abstract.label: IMPORTANCE
abstract.text: Pulmonary hypertension (PH), a progressive and life-threatening condition with rising prevalence among older adults, frequently coexists with systemic hypertension, the prognostic impact of which is poorly understood.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To evaluate the association between systemic hypertension and survival in patients with PH.

abstract.label: DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: This multicenter cohort study analyzed data from the Pulmonary Vascular Research Institute GoDeep meta-registry, integrating global retrospective and prospective PH cohorts (n = 3238 in Europe, n = 3014 in North America, n = 96 in Africa, n = 802 in Asia, and n = 851 in Oceania). Survival was assessed using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models and adjusted for key confounders, with sensitivity analyses to validate robustness. Independent external validation was performed in a cohort in the UK. A total of 12 771 patients with incident PH (median [IQR] age, 65 [53-73] years; 7372 [58%] female) were diagnosed via right heart catheterization and comprehensive clinical data, encompassing PH groups 1-5 and all age categories. The study spans diagnosis decades from 1980 to 2020. Data were analyzed from February 2025 until September 2026.

abstract.label: EXPOSURES
abstract.text: Center-reported diagnosis of systemic hypertension, baseline systolic systemic arterial pressure (sSAP), and heart rate as well as longitudinal sSAP and heart rate trajectories.

abstract.label: MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES
abstract.text: All-cause mortality, adjusted for confounding variables, including age, PH group, antihypertensive and PH-specific medications, and cardiac index.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Higher baseline sSAP and preexisting systemic hypertension were independently associated with improved survival. Patients with hypertension exhibited a 26% reduced mortality hazard (hazard ratio [HR], 0.74; 95% CI, 0.68-0.79) compared to their counterparts without hypertension. Survival benefits correlated positively with increasing sSAP (80-180 mm Hg), remained consistent across PH groups and age groups, and were independent of antihypertensive and PH-specific medications. Elevated heart rate was associated with higher mortality. sSAP increments correlated with improved cardiac index and tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion. Decreased sSAP and higher heart rate during follow-up correlated with higher mortality. External validation in a separate UK cohort confirmed these findings.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE
abstract.text: In this global PH cohort, higher sSAP was associated with enhanced survival, while a higher baseline heart rate and declining systemic blood pressure during follow-up were significantly associated with increased mortality risk.

articles.conclusion: In this global PH cohort, higher sSAP was associated with enhanced survival, while a higher baseline heart rate and declining systemic blood pressure during follow-up were significantly associated with increased mortality risk.

articles.title: Pretransplant Pulmonary Hemodynamics, Explant Histology, and Primary Graft Dysfunction after Lung Transplantation for Silicosis

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Silicosis associated with progressive massive fibrosis (PMF) is a major cause of end-stage lung disease among workers in the artificial stone industry. Patients with PMF are increasingly referred for lung transplant (LTx) evaluation and there is emerging evidence of pulmonary hypertension (PH) in patients with advanced PMF.

abstract.label: RESEARCH QUESTION
abstract.text: Among patients with PMF referred for lung transplantation, what is the incidence of PH and what are accompanying histopathologic pulmonary vascular aberrations?

abstract.label: STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS
abstract.text: Retrospective single-center cohort study of prospectively-enrolled participants, providing granular data on the invasive hemodynamic profile of patients with silicosis-associated PMF, histopathologic data on pulmonary vascular aberrations, and clinical data on post-transplant complications. Clinical and sociodemographic variables were collected. Explanted lungs from patients with silicosis-associated PMF underwent detailed pulmonary vascular histopathologic review and were descriptively compared with PAH explants. The incidence of primary graft dysfunction (PGD) was evaluated and descriptive analysis performed to provide associations of clinical features and PGD incidence.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: PH was present in over 95% of 21 patients with silicosis-associated PMF who underwent LTx, with a hemodynamic profile similar to patients transplanted for PAH. . Silicosis explants showed confluent silicotic nodules, extensive fibrosis and hyalinization, obscuration or obliteration of vascular structures, and perivascular fibrohistiocytic infiltrates with extrinsic narrowing. Classic PAH-type arteriolar muscular hypertrophy and plexiform arteriopathy were uncommon. In exploratory comparisons, patients who developed PGD had more frequent pretransplant right ventricular dysfunction (71% vs 21%; risk difference 0.50, 95% CI 0.06-0.75) and a lower median TAPSE/RVSP ratio (0.27 vs 0.39; Hedges' g -0.93, 95% CI -1.88 to 0.02) than in those without PGD.

abstract.label: INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: These findings suggest that PH in advanced silicosis with PMF is very common and represents a distinct pulmonary vascular phenotype characterized by extensive fibrotic vascular obliteration rather than the classic arteriopathy seen in PAH.

articles.conclusion: These findings suggest that PH in advanced silicosis with PMF is very common and represents a distinct pulmonary vascular phenotype characterized by extensive fibrotic vascular obliteration rather than the classic arteriopathy seen in PAH.

articles.title: Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging in the Diagnosis and Management of Postpartum Choriocarcinoma With Cardiopulmonary Complications

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (choriocarcinoma) may be associated with substantial diagnostic delay because of nonspecific symptoms and the rarity of this malignancy.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: A young postpartum woman presented with progressive dyspnea, fever, and chest pain. Delayed diagnosis led to clinical deterioration with severe pulmonary hypertension (PH), right ventricular (RV) dysfunction, culminating in cardiac arrest with successful resuscitation. Ultrasound demonstrating uterine lesions and markedly elevated β-human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) levels established the diagnosis of gestational choriocarcinoma. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) precisely assessed RV function and PH-related cardiac involvement. Chemotherapy normalized β-hCG levels and resolved PH and RV dysfunction.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: This case illustrates the diagnostic challenges of unclear dyspnea and choriocarcinoma complicated by PH and the value of CMR.

abstract.label: TAKE-HOME MESSAGE
abstract.text: CMR plays an important role in the assessment of cardiopulmonary complications of choriocarcinoma, although a structured evaluation of dyspnea, including β-hCG, is essential for the early diagnosis.

articles.title: D-dimer/NT-proBNP ratio in acute pulmonary embolism patients stratifies risk of chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: There are ongoing efforts to identify patients at risk of chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) during acute pulmonary embolism (APE). Lower D-dimer levels and right heart overload at APE diagnosis were reported to predict CTEPH. We hypothesised that plasma D-dimer to N-terminal pro-B type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) ratio assessed during APE may be useful for early CTEPH screening.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We followed 342 APE survivors (median age 64.5 years, female 56.1%), for a median of 39 (25-64) months.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Despite ≥3 months anticoagulation CTEPH was diagnosed in 22 (6.4%) patients (CTEPH(+)). At APE diagnosis, CTEPH(+) compared with subjects without this sequela (CTEPH(-)) presented with advanced right ventricular overload: increased tricuspid regurgitation peak gradient (TRPG) (46.5 mmHg versus 32.0 mmHg; p<0.001) and NT-proBNP (1860 ng·L-1 versus 515 ng·L-1; p=0.02). Despite no differences in plasma D-dimer (4210 μg·L-1 versus 5330 μg·L-1; p=0.10), the ratio of D-dimer to NT-proBNP (DD/NT-proBNP) was significantly lower in the CTEPH(+) cohort versus the CTEPH(-) cohort (2.89 μg·ng-1 versus 12.0 μg·ng-1; p<0.001). In patients with DD/NT-proBNP≤10 CTEPH was diagnosed in 20 cases (11.7%), whereas in the group with DD/NT-proBNP> 10 CTEPH could only be detected in 2 of 171 cases (1.2%) with an OR 0.09 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.02-0.38; p=0.0013), a sensitivity of 90.9% (95% CI 70.8-98.9%), a specificity 52.8% (95% CI 47.2-58.4%), a negative predictive value 98.8% (95% CI 95.8-99.9%), a and positive predictive value of 11.7% (95% CI 7.3-17.5%). Combination of DD/NT-proBNP≤10 with TRPG≥36 mmHg detected in 87 patients, including 17 patients with CTEPH (19.5% CTEPH incidence).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: DD/NT-proBNP>10 μg·ng-1 identifies patients with a low risk of subsequent CTEPH diagnosis, whereas DD/NT-proBNP≤10, especially presenting TRPG≥36 mmHg at echocardiography, forms a high risk group at follow-up.

articles.conclusion: DD/NT-proBNP>10 μg·ng-1 identifies patients with a low risk of subsequent CTEPH diagnosis, whereas DD/NT-proBNP≤10, especially presenting TRPG≥36 mmHg at echocardiography, forms a high risk group at follow-up.

articles.title: Exercise Right Atrial Stiffness From Pressure-Volume Loops and Prognosis in Pulmonary Hypertension

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: In pulmonary hypertension (PH), risk assessment focuses on right ventricular function and may overlook exercise-related right atrial (RA) functional limitation. We investigated whether RA stiffness during exercise reflects impaired right-heart filling reserve and is associated with prognosis beyond conventional measures.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We prospectively enrolled 68 participants in this observational study, including 42 with precapillary PH. Participants who had PH ruled out and patients with postcapillary PH formed reference groups. Participants underwent 3-dimensional echocardiography, right heart catheterization, and invasive RA pressure-volume loop analysis at rest and during standardized semisupine exercise. RA filling stiffness was derived from the reservoir phase. Patients with precapillary PH were stratified by median exercise RA filling stiffness.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: At rest, high- and low-stiffness groups had comparable right ventricular function, afterload, and cardiac index, but the high-stiffness group exhibited impaired phasic RA strain and venous congestion (median [interquartile range] liver stiffness, 7.1 [6.0-8.8] versus 5.2 [4.8-5.8] kPa; P=0.021). During exercise, mean RA pressure increased similarly, but the high-stiffness group had impaired peak cardiac index (3.3±1.0 versus 4.1±0.9 L/min per m2; P=0.015) and RA strain. Unlike resting RA stiffness, high exercise RA stiffness was independently associated with mortality (adjusted hazard ratio, 4.37 [95% CI, 1.20-15.96]). A model including RA conduit strain and right ventricular functional reserve discriminated high RA stiffness (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.90).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: RA stiffness during exercise integrates resting congestion with limited cardiac reserve and unmasks mortality risk missed by resting metrics. RA conduit strain and right ventricular functional reserve noninvasively identify the high-stiffness subgroup.

articles.conclusion: RA stiffness during exercise integrates resting congestion with limited cardiac reserve and unmasks mortality risk missed by resting metrics. RA conduit strain and right ventricular functional reserve noninvasively identify the high-stiffness subgroup.

articles.title: Shock With Acute Myocardial Dysfunction in Stercoral Colitis: Diagnosis and Management

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Shock in sepsis is predominantly vasodilatory; however, concomitant myocardial dysfunction may result in superimposed cardiogenic shock and a mixed shock state.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: A 75-year-old man with Parkinson disease, severe constipation, and stercoral colitis presented with profound shock after an enema. Echocardiography showed new biventricular dysfunction with regional wall-motion abnormalities. Invasive hemodynamic assessment demonstrated elevated filling pressures, low cardiac index, and low systemic vascular resistance despite substantial vasoactive and inotropic support, consistent with a mixed vasodilatory and cardiogenic shock. He improved after antibiotics and vasoactive support, but manual disimpaction after stabilization was followed within minutes by recurrent/similar shock.

abstract.label: REVIEW SUMMARY
abstract.text: This case illustrates a practical approach to mixed shock with acute myocardial dysfunction. Treatment of underlying infection should occur in parallel with characterization of the hemodynamic phenotype. Serial echocardiography and invasive hemodynamic assessment can identify concomitant vasodilatory and cardiogenic shock and guide circulatory support as shock physiology evolves.

abstract.label: TAKE-HOME MESSAGES
abstract.text: Shock physiology is dynamic. In patients with sepsis, serial clinical, echocardiographic, and hemodynamic reassessment can identify concomitant cardiogenic shock and guide circulatory support.

articles.title: Not All PVR Reductions Are Created Equal: Lessons From the CADENCE Trial
articles.journal: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation

abstract.text: The CADENCE trial evaluated sotatercept in combined post- and pre-capillary pulmonary hypertension associated with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (CpcPH-HFpEF). We analyzed the pathophysiological implications of the observed pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) reduction.A hemodynamic comparison was conducted contrasting the mechanistic effects of sotaercept with conventional pulmonary vasodilators.In CADENCE, PVR and pressure reductions occurred without marked cardiac output augmentation, contrasting with flow-mediated recruitment typical of traditional vasodilators. Sotatercept-induced PVR reduction may reflect true vascular reverse remodeling rather than vasodilation, underscoring the need to discriminate resistance reduction mechanisms in CpcPHHFpEF.

articles.title: Novel cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging biomarkers to track response to treatment including Sotatercept in a patient with idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension: a case report

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) causes progressive right ventricular (RV) pressure overload and left ventricular (LV) underfilling. Sotatercept is an activin-signal inhibitor, approved by FDA in 2024 and EMA in 2025, as an add-on treatment in adult patients with PAH. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR)-derived atrioventricular plane displacement (AVPD) and left ventricular pressure-volume (PV) loops may represent non-invasive markers of treatment response, particularly important as novel therapies addressing remodelling emerge.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: A 30-year-old woman was diagnosed with idiopathic PAH, after presenting with dyspnoea and peripheral oedema. Baseline CMR showed severe RV dilation, reduced RV ejection fraction, and low indexed LV stroke volume, with reduced bilateral AVPD and markedly impaired LV PV loop indices, with low stroke work, low mean external power, and high ventriculo-arterial coupling. Initial dual PAH therapy, with an endothelin receptor antagonist and a phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitor initially improved symptoms, pulmonary vascular resistance, as well as AVPD and PV loop derived indices, whereas conventional CMR indices showed only minimal change. One year later, despite triple therapy, including prostacyclin analogue, the patient deteriorated clinically and CMR showed worsening of AVPD and PV loop indices. Treatment escalation with Sotatercept immediately improved clinical status, haemodynamic, AVPD, and PV loop indices despite persistent RV remodelling.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Serial CMR-derived AVPD and LV PV loops may provide clinically useful additional information during longitudinal follow-up of PAH patients, especially in those approaching maximal available medical therapies. In the present case, both AVPD and LV PV loops reflected treatment response, and showed significant improvement after initiation of Sotatercept.

articles.title: Resolution of Lancisi's sign following bicaval TricValve implantation for torrential tricuspid regurgitation: a case report defining a novel bedside marker of haemodynamic recovery

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Caval valve implantation (CAVI) using the TricValve system is an emerging treatment option for severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) in patients who are unsuitable for surgery or orthotopic transcatheter intervention. Lancisi's sign is a classical manifestation of severe TR; however, its resolution after CAVI has not been described.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: An 85-year-old woman with recurrent right heart failure and torrential TR presented with prominent bilateral Lancisi's sign. Echocardiography revealed severe annular dilatation (48 mm), right ventricular dysfunction (TAPSE, 13 mm), and a left ventricular ejection fraction of 40%. Owing to prohibitive surgical risk (EuroSCORE II 18.4%; TRI SCORE 14), she underwent successful implantation of 29-mm superior vena cava and 35-mm inferior vena cava TricValve prostheses. At 3 months, Lancisi's sign had completely resolved, NYHA functional class improved from III-IV to I-II, NT-proBNP decreased from 25 000 to 2 000 pg/mL, TAPSE increased from 13 to 20 mm, and no rehospitalization or device-related adverse event occurred. We report a structured single-patient case using clinical examination, echocardiography, invasive hemodynamic assessment, laboratory markers, and 3-month follow-up after bicaval TricValve implantation.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Bicaval TricValve implantation resulted in marked symptomatic, biochemical, echocardiographic, and bedside clinical improvements. The resolution of Lancisi's sign may represent a simple marker of hemodynamic recovery after CAVI.

articles.title: Pulmonary Hypertension and Its Association With Cardiac Transplant Outcomes: Does Pulmonary Artery Systolic Pressure Matter?
Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists in Obese Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: To evaluate whether GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1) receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), compared with DPP4 (dipeptidyl peptidase-4) inhibitors or sulfonylureas, are associated with reduced all-cause mortality or heart failure hospitalizations in patients with obesity and type 2 diabetes, and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: PRAISE-HFpEF (Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonist in Obese Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction) was a nationwide multicenter cohort study using a new-user, active-comparator design within the national Veterans Affairs Health System (170 US hospitals). Adults with type 2 diabetes between January 1, 2000 and December 31, 2021, were identified from centralized electronic health records. Patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and a body mass index ≥30 kg/m2 were selected using a validated diagnostic algorithm. Exposure was initiation of a GLP-1RA versus DPP4 inhibitors/sulfonylurea from January 1, 2015 to December 31, 2021. The primary outcome was time to all-cause mortality or heart failure hospitalization. Inverse probability of treatment weighting based on the propensity score was used to balanced baseline characteristics.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 179 288 patients with type 2 diabetes, obesity, and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, 1024 GLP-1RA users and 796 DPP4 inhibitors/sulfonylurea users met inclusion criteria. Over a median follow-up of 1.5 years, GLP-1RA use was associated with a lower risk of the primary outcome (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.78 [95% CI, 0.64-0.95], P=0.01). Weight loss was modestly greater with GLP-1RAs compared with DPP4 inhibitors/sulfonylurea (-12.9% versus -10.1%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Among patients with obese heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and type 2 diabetes, GLP-1RA initiation was associated with a lower incidence of death or heart failure hospitalization compared with alternative oral agents.

articles.conclusion: Among patients with obese heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and type 2 diabetes, GLP-1RA initiation was associated with a lower incidence of death or heart failure hospitalization compared with alternative oral agents.

articles.title: Efficacy of empagliflozin in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction according to the presence of echocardiographic features of diastolic dysfunction in the EMPEROR-Preserved trial

abstract.label: AIMS
abstract.text: To define the impact of diastolic dysfunction (DD) on the response to empagliflozin treatment in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.

abstract.label: METHODS AND RESULTS
abstract.text: Diastolic dysfunction was defined by left atrial volume index ≥34 ml/m2, the ratio of early diastolic mitral inflow velocity to early diastolic mitral annular tissue velocity (E/e) ≥ 13 or left ventricular mass index >115 (males) or >95 (females). We created three categories of increasing DD (0, 1, or ≥2 DD criteria at baseline) to describe the effect of DD on response to empagliflozin therapy and adverse effects. Of 5988 patients in the EMPEROR-Preserved trial, 3766 (63%) had no documented baseline DD, 1619 (27%) had one, and 603 (10%) had two or more measures. Baseline DD was associated with sex, race, ethnicity, and region and was more common with lower heart rate, DBP, body weight, and eGFR. Despite baseline DD not being significantly associated with the primary endpoint of hospitalization for heart failure or cardiovascular death within the placebo group, a progressive treatment effect across the three DD categories was seen (trend test P-value .0014), with estimated hazard ratios of empagliflozin vs placebo of 0.91 (none present), 0.64 (1 present), and 0.49 (≥2). A significant treatment-by-subgroup trend test was also observed for the total number of hospitalizations for heart failure. Both Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score improvement at week 52 and safety profile were consistent across DD categories.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Baseline detection of echocardiographic DD predicted improved clinical response to empagliflozin in a graded fashion, but the reasons cannot be reliably determined from this analysis.

articles.conclusion: Baseline detection of echocardiographic DD predicted improved clinical response to empagliflozin in a graded fashion, but the reasons cannot be reliably determined from this analysis.

articles.title: Controversy: Atrial fibrillation ablation should be performed in patients with HFpEF
articles.journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology

abstract.text: The role of atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation in the management of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) remains an under investigated issue with no robust clinical trials data. This controversy reviews the evidence for and against AF ablation in this complex condition from two different perspectives reviewing mechanistic and observational evidence aswell as proposing future directions for research in the field.

articles.title: Renal Decline Before Heart Transplantation in Left Ventricular Assist Device-Supported Recipients: United Network for Organ Sharing Analysis
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)

abstract.text: Although baseline renal impairment and post-heart transplantation (HT) dialysis are established clinical predictors, the prognostic impact of pre-HT renal decline in patients bridged with left ventricular assist devices (LVADs) remains unclear. We retrospectively analyzed patients from the United Network for Organ Sharing registry who underwent HT following LVAD support between 2009 and 2024. Renal decline was defined as a greater than or equal to 40% reduction in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) from listing to HT. Among 10,454 patients, 624 (6.0%) experienced pre-HT renal decline. Patients with renal decline had longer waitlist durations (median 297 vs. 197 days; p < 0.001), lower eGFR at HT (42.0 vs. 70.6 ml/min/1.73 m2; p < 0.001), and higher rates of post-HT dialysis (23.7 vs. 12.8%; p < 0.001). Independent predictors of renal decline included longer waitlist time and perioperative blood transfusions, whereas HeartMate 3 LVAD use was protective. Renal decline was independently associated with an increased risk of post-HT dialysis (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]: 2.64) and all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR]: 1.16), with post-HT dialysis strongly predicting mortality (aHR: 3.48). Renal deterioration is a significant predictor of post-HT dialysis and mortality in LVAD-bridged patients. Incorporating renal trajectory into risk stratification may enhance candidate selection and promote perioperative renal protection strategies.

articles.title: Current Global Trends and Challenges of Pediatric Ventricular Assist Device Programs: An ACTION Collaborative Survey
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)

abstract.text: Ventricular assist devices (VADs) have become an established therapy for children with end-stage heart failure, yet multinational data describing pediatric VAD programs remain limited. We conducted a 12 question survey through the Advanced Cardiac Therapies Improving Outcomes Network (ACTION) involving 74 international healthcare professionals from pediatric VAD programs outside North America. The survey assessed device and resource availability, multidisciplinary team composition, program challenges, and future priorities. Fifteen responses representing 15 centers from 14 countries were received, including 13 centers with established pediatric VAD programs. Most centers (91%, 10/11) managed 1-5 pediatric VAD patients annually. Berlin Heart EXCOR and HeartMate 3 were available in 85% (11/13) of centers, while only 46.7% (7/15) had a dedicated VAD coordinator. Major barriers included inadequate education for intensive care unit (ICU) and nursing staff and patients (69%, 9/13), financial constraints (54%, 7/13), limited device availability (46%, 6/13), and lack of outpatient VAD experience, with 31% (4/13) of centers reporting no experience discharging patients on VAD support. Substantial variation in device availability, multidisciplinary resources, and program experience exists across regions. These findings highlight important gaps in pediatric VAD care and support international collaboration to improve education, infrastructure, and access to advanced heart failure therapies.

articles.title: Coronary angiography in heart transplants from donors older than 40: a Eurotransplant study

abstract.label: BACKGROUND AND AIMS
abstract.text: The increasing age of heart donors in Europe raises concerns about undetected coronary artery disease (CAD), a contributor to early graft dysfunction and long-term complications. This study examined the association between donor coronary angiography (CA) and heart transplant utilization, particularly in donors aged >40 years.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A total of 20 681 donor heart offers reported to Eurotransplant between 2004 and 2020 were analysed. The use of CA, donor characteristics, and acceptance rates were assessed. CAD status was imputed for donors without angiography using logistic regression based on clinical risk factors. Transplantation probabilities were modelled using observed and imputed CAD severity to explore potential differences under a scenario of broader CA availability.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: CA was performed in 23.5% of cases, predominantly in older donors and those with cardiovascular risk factors. Among donors with CA, 37.5% had CAD, which was significantly associated with age, male sex, hypertension, and smoking. Donors with normal CA findings had lower odds of rejection compared with those without CA (odds ratio 0.36, P < .0001). In a counterfactual model, broader CA availability in donors aged >40 years was associated with a higher estimated transplant utilization (56.4%-67.1%), corresponding to a model-based increase of ∼535 transplants.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In this observational cohort, CA availability was associated with differences in donor heart utilization, particularly when findings were normal or showed non-significant CAD. These findings suggest that angiographic information may reduce diagnostic uncertainty and support clinical decision-making in older donors. A risk-adapted, resource-sensitive approach to CA use is warranted.

articles.conclusion: In this observational cohort, CA availability was associated with differences in donor heart utilization, particularly when findings were normal or showed non-significant CAD. These findings suggest that angiographic information may reduce diagnostic uncertainty and support clinical decision-making in older donors. A risk-adapted, resource-sensitive approach to CA use is warranted.

articles.title: Restoring Coronary Vasomotion in Pediatric Cardiac Allograft Vasculopathy: A Bioadaptor-Based Interventional Strategy

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Percutaneous coronary interventions in cardiac allograft vasculopathy (CAV) remain challenging. In CAV, diffuse neointimal proliferation contributes to progressive allograft dysfunction and increased mortality. Although second-generation drug-eluting stents are widely utilized, permanent vessel caging may limit adaptive remodeling, resulting in target lesion failure. Drug-eluting coronary bioadaptors have been designed to provide vessel support while enabling restoration of physiological vasomotion.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: We report the case of a 15-year-old male patient with CAV, 4 years after heart transplantation. A DynamX drug-eluting coronary bioadaptor was successfully implanted in the circumflex artery. At 20-month follow-up, coronary angiography and intravascular ultrasound demonstrated preserved vessel patency and compliance, with no evidence of target lesion failure.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: This case highlights the feasibility of bioadaptor-based percutaneous coronary interventions in a pediatric heart transplant recipient with CAV and supports further evaluation of this technology in patients with complex coronary lesions.

abstract.label: TAKE-HOME MESSAGE
abstract.text: Bioadaptors may provide acute vessel support while allowing dynamic vessel motion after uncaging in CAV.

articles.title: Idiopathic Middle Aortic Syndrome Causing Pediatric Resistant Hypertension: Beyond Coarctation

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Middle aortic syndrome (MAS) is a rare cause of severe hypertension in children, characterized by segmental narrowing of the distal thoracic and abdominal aorta. Early recognition is essential to prevent irreversible end-organ damage.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: A 12-year-old girl presented with resistant hypertension, headache, facial edema, blurred vision, and postprandial abdominal pain. Marked upper-to-lower limb blood pressure discrepancy, with absent femoral pulses. Computed tomography angiography demonstrated long-segment thoracoabdominal aortic narrowing extending to the iliac arteries, consistent with MAS. Because of unfavorable anatomy for endovascular treatment. Thoracoabdominal extra-anatomic aorto-aortic bypass with polytetrafluoroethylene graft was successfully performed.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: This case highlights the diagnostic challenge of idiopathic MAS and demonstrates that individualized management based on vascular anatomy can achieve excellent outcomes.

abstract.label: TAKE-HOME MESSAGES
abstract.text: Cross-sectional vascular imaging should be considered in children with resistant hypertension and diminished femoral pulses. Open aorto-aortic bypass remains effective when endovascular treatment is unsuitable.

articles.title: Heart failure therapy in congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries: effect on right ventricular function and survival

abstract.label: BACKGROUND AND AIMS
abstract.text: The aim of the study was to assess the effect of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) on cardiac function, neurohormonal activation, and mortality in adults with congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries (cc-TGA) presenting with systemic right ventricular (RV) systolic dysfunction. The study hypothesis was that GDMT use (assessed using the GDMT score) was associated with improved cardiac function (higher RV free wall strain [RVFWS]), less neurohormonal activation (lower N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide [NT-proBNP] levels), and lower mortality.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: GDMT score, RVFWS, and NT-proBNP levels were assessed at baseline and 1-year follow-up. GDMT uptitration was assessed using ΔGDMT (GDMT at 1-year minus GDMT at baseline). Improvements in RV systolic function and neurohormonal activation were defined as a relative increase in RVFWS of >20% and a relative decrease in NT-proBNP levels of >20%, respectively.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 213 patients (age 43 ± 15 years; 54% male), baseline GDMT score was 1.97 ± 1.27, and ΔGDMT score was 0.74 ± 0.39. Baseline RVFWS was -18 ± 5%; 25% had improved RV systolic function. Baseline NT-proBNP was 369 (142, 1004) pg/mL; 56% had improved neurohormonal activation. Higher baseline GDMT score and ΔGDMT score were associated with improvement in RV systolic function and neurohormonal activation. Overall, 34 (16%) patients died, and higher baseline GDMT score and ΔGDMT score were associated with a lower risk of mortality and of the composite adverse event endpoint (heart failure hospitalization, death, and heart transplantation). Clinical benefits of GDMT use were observed only in patients with moderate/severe RV systolic dysfunction, and not in patients with mild RV systolic dysfunction.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: GDMT use was associated with improved outcomes in patients with moderate/severe RV systolic dysfunction.

articles.conclusion: GDMT use was associated with improved outcomes in patients with moderate/severe RV systolic dysfunction.

articles.title: Obesity, frail obesity, and outcomes after durable left ventricular assist device implantation: a pooled analysis of the MOMENTUM 3 trials

abstract.label: BACKGROUND AND AIMS
abstract.text: Obesity in patients supported by left ventricular assist devices (LVADs) is linked to excess mortality and haemocompatibility-related events. Whether this association persists with the fully magnetically levitated HeartMate 3 (HM3) pump is unknown. This analysis tested outcomes with obesity and the additive influence of co-existing frailty ('frail obesity') in the contemporary era.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The study pooled 2200 HM3 recipients from the MOMENTUM 3 pivotal randomized trial (n = 515) and Continued Access Protocol (n = 1685). Obesity was defined as body mass index (BMI) ≥30 kg/m2 and frailty by a 40-item Rockwood cumulative-deficit frailty index (FI), with clinically relevant frailty defined as FI ≥0.325 (moderate-severe frailty); BMI was excluded from the FI to avoid mathematical coupling. The primary endpoint was survival to transplant, recovery, or 24 months of support free of disabling stroke (modified Rankin score >3) or pump replacement reoperation.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Obese patients (n = 887, 40.3%) were younger, less often with ischaemic aetiology, and more frequently women, but more often had diabetes and hypertension, than non-obese patients. Unadjusted 2-year outcomes were similar between groups (freedom from the primary endpoint: 75.1% vs 77.1%, log-rank P = .34; survival: 79.9% vs 81.2%, P = .57). After covariate adjustment, obesity was independently associated with a higher risk of the primary endpoint (hazard ratio [HR] 1.30, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.07-1.58) and all-cause mortality (HR 1.35, 95% CI 1.10-1.67), as well as heart failure hospitalization, infection, and arrhythmia, but not stroke, bleeding, or early right heart failure. Frailty affected 67.3% of obese recipients (571/849) and was associated with a higher adjusted risk of the primary endpoint (HR 1.51, 95% CI 1.09-2.10), overall mortality and non-haemocompatibilty-related morbidity endpoints. The obesity-by-frailty interaction was not significant for either the primary endpoint (P = .436) or mortality (P = .215), indicating additive rather than synergistic risk; frail-obese patients nonetheless carried the highest absolute risk of any subgroup. Frailty improved by at least one severity class by 6 months in 75.9% of frail-obese patients, and improvement was associated with better survival (adjusted HR 0.14, 95% CI 0.07-0.26).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In the HM3 era, obese and non-obese recipients had similar unadjusted 2-year outcomes; however, after adjustment for baseline case-mix, obesity was independently associated with a higher risk of both the primary endpoint and all-cause mortality, together with heart failure hospitalization, infection, and arrhythmia. Frailty was independently associated with adverse outcomes across nearly all endpoints and was highly prevalent among obese recipients; the combination of obesity and frailty was additive but not synergistic, with frail-obese patients carrying the highest absolute risk. Frailty, however, proved substantially reversible after LVAD support, and its improvement was associated with markedly better survival. Obesity and frailty should therefore be assessed together, rather than through BMI thresholds alone, with recognition that frailty status is dynamic after implantation and that improvement in frailty is associated with markedly better survival.

articles.conclusion: In the HM3 era, obese and non-obese recipients had similar unadjusted 2-year outcomes; however, after adjustment for baseline case-mix, obesity was independently associated with a higher risk of both the primary endpoint and all-cause mortality, together with heart failure hospitalization, infection, and arrhythmia.
