articles.title: High-Grade Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage Complicated by Refractory Cardiogenic Shock Successfully Treated With Microaxial Flow Pump

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) is complicated by Takotsubo syndrome (TTS) in 15% to 25% of patients. Managed with supportive care, TTS with refractory cardiogenic shock represents a challenging complication with limited published guidance.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: A 78-year-old woman presented with high-grade aSAH requiring external ventricular drain placement, stent-assisted aneurysm coiling, and dual antiplatelet therapy complicated by TTS and cardiogenic shock refractory to pressors and inotropes. A microaxial flow pump (Impella 5.5) was deployed, with full myocardial and neurological recovery.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Often self-limiting but causing secondary injury, TTS secondary to neurologic injury is driven by catecholamine-mediated myocardial injury. Mechanical circulatory support has been reported for TTS and refractory cardiogenic shock. After conducting a literature review, we believe this is the first reported use of an Impella 5.5 for refractory cardiogenic shock from TTS secondary to subarachnoid hemorrhage.

abstract.label: TAKE-HOME MESSAGE
abstract.text: Microaxial flow pump rescue appears to be a viable strategy for refractory cardiogenic shock complicating high-grade aSAH, even during dual-antiplatelet therapy.

articles.title: Multisite Peripheral Photoplethysmography Captures Intra-Aortic Balloon Pump Counterpulsation and Weaning State in Cardiogenic Shock

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) counterpulsation raises aortic diastolic pressure every cycle (1:1) or alternate cycles (1:2, weaning). Whether they reach peripheral photoplethysmography (PPG) is unknown; 1 report described 1:1 only.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: An 82-year-old man in IABP-supported cardiogenic shock had finger and thenar PPG on 1:1, 1:2, removal, and twice afterward. An augmented diastolic peak appeared on every finger beat on 1:1 and alternate beats on 1:2, barring ectopy, and none afterward. Perfusion index reached a nadir at removal and rose through recovery; finger-thenar coherence followed a similar trend.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Peripheral PPG encoded assist ratio and weaning state. The augmented peak was proportionally larger at the finger than in the aorta, raising the hypothesis that it reflects root- and arch-supplied territories.

abstract.label: TAKE-HOME MESSAGE
abstract.text: Ordinary peripheral PPG carries a beat-resolved signature of IABP counterpulsation and of the weaning course, without vascular access.

articles.title: Hydralazine-isosorbide dinitrate in chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction: the H-HeFT trial

abstract.label: BACKGROUND AND AIMS
abstract.text: Hydralazine-isosorbide dinitrate (H-ISDN) has shown benefit in earlier randomized trials of patients with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and chronic heart failure. This trial tested if H-ISDN could reduce worsening heart failure or mortality in patients with chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) receiving contemporary treatment.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The Hydralazine-Isosorbide Dinitrate in Patients With Chronic Heart Failure Trial (H-HeFT) was a multicentre, randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in patients with HFrEF at 23 Danish hospitals (New York Heart Association class II-IV, elevated N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide and LVEF ≤40%). Target treatment was hydralazine 75 mg/isosorbide dinitrate 40 mg three times a day (t.i.d). The primary endpoint was a composite of hospitalization with worsening heart failure, an urgent outpatient visit resulting in intravenous/metolazone therapy for heart failure, heart transplantation, left ventricular assist device implantation, or death. Secondary endpoints included components of the primary outcome.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Overall, 592 predominantly White patients (median age 72 years, 18% women) were randomized with a mean follow-up of 3.7 years. The primary outcome occurred in 90 of 294 patients (30.6%) in the H-ISDN group and in 91 of 298 patients (30.5%) in the placebo group [hazard ratio (HR) 0.90; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.67-1.21; P = .48]. There were 57 deaths in the H-ISDN group vs 72 in the placebo group (HR 0.72; 95% CI 0.51-1.02); worsening heart failure events occurred in 52 vs 47 patients (HR 1.01; 95% CI 0.68-1.50).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Hydralazine-isosorbide dinitrate did not change the incidence of the composite endpoint of heart failure events or death in patients with heart failure and LVEF ≤40%.

articles.conclusion: Hydralazine-isosorbide dinitrate did not change the incidence of the composite endpoint of heart failure events or death in patients with heart failure and LVEF ≤40%.

articles.title: Targeting ALDOA Lactylation Reverses Vascular Remodeling in Pulmonary Hypertension by Disrupting Actin Polymerization and YAP Activation

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Maladaptive vascular remodeling is a hallmark of pulmonary hypertension (PH), and therapeutic strategies directly targeting the pathological activity of smooth muscle cells remain limited. Metabolic and epigenetic dysregulation are established drivers of PH, and lysine lactylation has emerged as a novel posttranslational modification implicated in diverse diseases; however, its direct contribution to PH progression remains undefined.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Integrated lactylomic and proteomic profiling was performed in hypoxic human pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells. The functional role of ALDOA (aldolase A) lactylation at lysine 42 (K42) was assessed using site-specific mutant virus and smooth muscle cell-specific inducible ALDOA knockout mice in 2 established PH models: SU5416+hypoxia in mice and monocrotaline in rats.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: We identified ALDOA as a prominent lactylation target in hypoxic pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells, with K42 lactylation consistently elevated in primary pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells derived from PH rodent models and human PH tissues. Mechanistically, AARS1 (alanyl-tRNA synthetase 1)-mediated ALDOA K42 lactylation enhanced its binding to γ-actin, independent of glycolytic activity. This lactylation-enhanced interaction promoted F-actin polymerization and activated YAP (Yes-associated protein) signaling via LATS1 (large tumor suppressor kinase 1) inhibition, thereby driving pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cell proliferation and phenotypic switching. Moreover, YAP/TEAD4 (TEA domain transcription factor 4)-mediated transcriptional upregulation of AARS1 established a positive feedback loop reinforcing ALDOA K42 lactylation under hypoxia. In vivo, ALDOA inducible knockout or reconstitution with the lactylation-deficient K42R (lysine 42 mutant to arginine) mutant attenuated experimental PH progression, with suppressed F-actin/YAP activation and reduced vascular remodeling. Furthermore, competitive inhibition of lactylation through β‑alanine reduced ALDOA K42 lactylation and ameliorated vascular remodeling in ALDOA-overexpressing rodent PH models. Translationally, pharmacological disruption of the ALDOA/γ-actin interaction by raltegravir suppressed cytoskeletal reorganization and YAP signaling, mitigating PH progression in both mouse and rat models.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: AARS1-mediated ALDOA K42 lactylation drives pulmonary vascular remodeling through a mechanism independent of ALDOA's catalytic activity, promoting F-actin polymerization and YAP activation. Precision targeting of this modification selectively inhibits pathological signaling while preserving metabolic homeostasis, highlighting a translational potential for precision intervention in PH.

articles.conclusion: AARS1-mediated ALDOA K42 lactylation drives pulmonary vascular remodeling through a mechanism independent of ALDOA's catalytic activity, promoting F-actin polymerization and YAP activation. Precision targeting of this modification selectively inhibits pathological signaling while preserving metabolic homeostasis, highlighting a translational potential for precision intervention in PH.

articles.title: Prediction of Bailout Mechanical Circulatory Support Use for Hemodynamic Collapse During PCI: The ORACLE Score

abstract.text: Background: Bailout mechanical circulatory support (MCS) may be used in the setting of intraprocedural hemodynamic collapse during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). We developed and externally validated a simple risk prediction model for bailout MCS use for hemodynamic collapse during PCI. Methods: Consecutive patients undergoing PCI at a tertiary hospital between 2018 and 2025 were included in the derivation cohort (n=6,931), after excluding cases of salvage PCI and procedures performed with pre-existing or prophylactic MCS. The primary endpoint was bailout MCS use for hemodynamic collapse. A multivariable Firth logistic regression model was developed, internally validated, and translated into a simplified integer-based risk score (ORACLE). External validation was performed in 214,877 PCIs from the Blue Cross Blue Shield of Michigan Cardiovascular Consortium (BMC2) registry. Results: The incidence of bailout MCS was 1.4% in the derivation cohort. Six variables (non-elective presentation, systolic blood pressure, chronic heart failure, prior PCI, rotational/orbital atherectomy, and left main PCI) independently predicted the primary endpoint. The regression model demonstrated good discrimination both in the derivation (area under the curve [AUC] 0.817; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.774-0.860) and external validation (AUC 0.761; 95% CI 0.753-0.770) cohorts. The simplified ORACLE score preserved most of the discriminatory performance of the full model (AUC 0.791 in the derivation cohort and 0.718 in the external validation cohort) and effectively stratified patients, with observed bailout MCS rates ranging from 0.4% in the low-risk category to 8.7% in the high-risk group, with similar findings in the external validation cohort. Discrimination was consistent across clinically relevant subgroups. Negative predictive value was >99% in both the derivation and external validation cohorts. Conclusions:: ORACLE is a simple score to estimate the risk of bailout MCS use for hemodynamic collapse during PCI, which may support preprocedural risk assessment.

articles.title: Antecedent Kidney Function and Cardiovascular Mortality in Over 300 000 Patients With Incident Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Chronic kidney disease is a frequent comorbidity in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and has been proposed as a contributor to its development. However, the spectrum of antecedent kidney function before incident HFpEF and its association with subsequent cardiovascular outcomes remains unclear.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a multicenter cohort study across 170 US Veterans Affairs hospitals, including patients with incident HFpEF diagnosed between January 1, 2000, and June 30, 2025. HFpEF was ascertained using natural language processing-derived left ventricular ejection fraction ≥50% closest to the incident HF date and a validated HFpEF algorithm incorporating loop diuretic use, elevated natriuretic peptide levels, and an HFpEF-age, body mass index, and atrial fibrillation score >0.5. Antecedent kidney function was classified using 2 estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) measurements obtained ≥90 days apart before incident HFpEF and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio. We characterized antecedent kidney function, including albuminuria (urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio ≥30 mg/g), and examined its associations with 5-year cardiovascular death and heart failure hospitalization. Competing-risk analysis was performed accounting for noncardiovascular death as a competing event for cardiovascular death.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 304 712 patients meeting HFpEF ascertainment criteria, 236 910 comprised the final cohort; 51% had antecedent eGFR ≥60 mL/min per 1.73m2. Overall, 15% had an eGFR ≥90 mL/min per 1.73m2. Patients with eGFR <60 mL/min per 1.73m2 were older and had more diabetes and hypertension. 51% of the patients with eGFR <60 mL/min per 1.73m2 had body mass index <30 kg/m2, including 20% with body mass index <25 kg/m2. Progressively lower antecedent kidney function was associated with graded increases in cardiovascular death and heart failure hospitalization. Among decedents, the proportion of deaths attributed to cardiovascular causes increased from 25% in the preserved eGFR (≥90 mL/min per 1.73m2) without documented albuminuria to 32% with albuminuria and 38% with advanced kidney dysfunction (P<0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In this nationwide study of patients with incident HFpEF, antecedent kidney dysfunction was common but not uniformly present before HFpEF onset. Furthermore, among patients who developed HFpEF, antecedent kidney dysfunction identified a higher-risk phenotype, with progressively greater cardiovascular mortality and heart failure hospitalization with declining kidney function.

articles.conclusion: In this nationwide study of patients with incident HFpEF, antecedent kidney dysfunction was common but not uniformly present before HFpEF onset. Furthermore, among patients who developed HFpEF, antecedent kidney dysfunction identified a higher-risk phenotype, with progressively greater cardiovascular mortality and heart failure hospitalization with declining kidney function.

articles.title: Performance of the PREVENT-HF Equations Across Heart Failure Subtypes in Community-Based and Ambulatory Healthcare Samples

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The PREVENT-HF equations estimate 10-year risk of overall heart failure (HF), inclusive of both HF with preserved and reduced ejection fraction (HFpEF; HFrEF). Given differential risk factor profiles, pathophysiology, and therapeutic strategies for each HF subtype, we sought to examine the performance of PREVENT-HF for subtype-specific risk assessment.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We included data from five pooled longitudinal cohort studies (baseline exam 1989 to 2013) and two longitudinal primary-care electronic health record-based samples (Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center [BIDMC], baseline 2004 to 2014; Mass General Brigham [MGB], baseline 2001 to 2018). We assessed the performance of the PREVENT-HF equations in predicting 10-year incident HFrEF and HFpEF, including model discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUROC]; average precision [AP]/event rate) and calibration (integrated calibration index [ICI]), in adults aged 30-79 years without prevalent cardiovascular disease or HF.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The pooled cohort studies included 23,652 (55% women, age 60 ± 13 years), of whom 1,232 developed HF (432 [35%] HFpEF, 522 [42%] HFrEF). The BIDMC sample included 29,815 (55% women, 50 ± 13 years), of whom 259 (1%) developed HF (133 [51%] HFpEF, 101 [39%] HFrEF). MGB included 138,999 (62% women, 52 ± 13 years), of whom 1050 developed HF (586 [56%] HFpEF, 381 [36%] HFrEF). PREVENT-HF demonstrated better discrimination for HFpEF than HFrEF across all samples: in the pooled cohorts, the AUROC for HFpEF was 0.824 (95% CI 0.807, 0.839) versus 0.789 (95% CI 0.770, 0.807) for HFrEF; in BIDMC, the AUROC for HFpEF was 0.897 (95% CI 0.874, 0.918) versus 0.833 (95% CI 0.791, 0.869) for HFrEF; in MGB, the AUROC for HFpEF was 0.864 (95% CI 0.848, 0.880) versus 0.797 (95% CI 0.771, 0.820) for HFrEF. Similar results were reflected in the AP/event rate ratios: 2.92 (95% CI 2.47, 3.54) for HFpEF compared to 2.66 (95% CI 2.33, 3.14) for HFrEF in the pooled cohorts; 8.08 (95% CI 6.12, 12.30) for HFpEF compared to 5.12 (95% CI 3.84, 8.17) for HFrEF in BIDMC; and 6.84 (95% CI 5.66, 8.28) for HFpEF compared to 4.12 (95% CI 3.37, 5.16) for HFrEF in MGB. Calibration was similar for HFpEF and HFrEF across samples. For example, in the pooled cohorts, the ICI for HFpEF was 0.041 (95% CI 0.039, 0.043) and for HFrEF was 0.038 (95% CI 0.036, 0.040).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: PREVENT-HF demonstrated excellent discrimination for both HF subtypes across community-based cohorts and real-world samples, with consistently better discrimination for HFpEF as compared to HFrEF. Given PREVENT-HF was developed to estimate overall HF risk rather than subtype-specific risk, future studies are needed to establish subtype-specific risk thresholds.

articles.conclusion: PREVENT-HF demonstrated excellent discrimination for both HF subtypes across community-based cohorts and real-world samples, with consistently better discrimination for HFpEF as compared to HFrEF. Given PREVENT-HF was developed to estimate overall HF risk rather than subtype-specific risk, future studies are needed to establish subtype-specific risk thresholds.

articles.title: Ventricular Arrhythmia After Percutaneous Edge-to-Edge Tricuspid Valve Repair

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) treats severe tricuspid regurgitation, but electrical complications from device-tissue interactions remain poorly characterized.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: A 79-year-old woman developed postural ventricular arrhythmias after TriClip implantation. Electrocardiography was consistent with an ectopic origin in the posterior/inferior right ventricle, anatomically concordant with the posteroseptal clip. Orthostatic reduction in right ventricular volume may have induced dynamic clip-endocardium contact. Saline infusion abolished the arrhythmias. At 1 month, she remained asymptomatic despite unchanged device-to-septum distance on supine echocardiography, suggesting stabilization of the device-tissue interface over time.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: As the first reported case of postural arrhythmia from mechanical TriClip-septal interaction, this addresses a gap in TEER literature regarding how orthostatic volume shifts trigger device-related complications.

abstract.label: TAKE-HOME MESSAGES
abstract.text: Orthostatic volume shifts may provoke dynamic device-tissue contact and arrhythmias post-TEER. Careful clip positioning and vigilant postprocedural monitoring are essential, and stabilization of the device-tissue interface over time may allow conservative management.

articles.title: Acquired Gerbode Defect After TAVR Presenting With Severe Acute Liver and Kidney Injury

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Acquired Gerbode defects after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) are rare and may present atypically, delaying diagnosis.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: A 71-year-old man presented 15 days after TAVR with severe acute liver and kidney injury despite preserved ventricular systolic function and normal prosthetic valve function on transthoracic echocardiography. Right heart catheterization revealed elevated filling pressures, an oxygen saturation step-up from the superior vena cava (51%) to the pulmonary artery (79%), and a pulmonary/systemic flow ratio of 2.9. Transesophageal echocardiography identified a high-pressure left ventricular-to-right atrial shunt through the membranous septum. Residual shunting after transcatheter closure caused severe intravascular hemolysis and necessitated surgical salvage. The postoperative course was complicated by multiorgan failure and death.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: This case highlights an atypical presentation of an acquired Gerbode defect. Complementary transesophageal echocardiography and invasive hemodynamic assessment were essential for diagnosis.

abstract.label: TAKE-HOME MESSAGE
abstract.text: Occult intracardiac shunting should be considered after TAVR when severe end-organ dysfunction is discordant with reassuring transthoracic echocardiographic findings.

articles.title: Updated Staging System to Define Cardiogenic Shock Severity A Cardiogenic Shock Working Group Report

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Cardiogenic shock (CS) severity is defined by the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions stages and modifications from the Cardiogenic Shock Working Group (CSWG). Lactate thresholds, treatment intensity, and cardiac arrest modifiers remain incompletely defined. We aimed to refine the 2022 CSWG staging criteria using contemporary data.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Patients with CS from heart failure (HF-CS) or myocardial infarction (MI-CS) enrolled in the multicenter CSWG registry (2021-2025) were analyzed. Associations between systolic blood pressure (SBP), lactate, treatment intensity, and in-hospital mortality, which is considered a surrogate for CS severity, were examined. External application of the updated system was performed in an independent US health system.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 11,640 patients (60.5% HF-CS, 26.1% MI-CS), SBP and lactate demonstrated graded relationships with mortality across thresholds (SBP <60, 60-<90, ≥90 mm Hg; lactate 0-2, >2-5, >5-10, >10 mmol/L). Mortality increased incrementally with treatment intensity. The 2026 staging system, incorporating these thresholds and the number of vasoactive drugs and temporary mechanical circulatory support devices (stage C: 1-2, D: 3-4, E: ≥5), demonstrated progressive mortality across stages. Compared with previous CSWG staging, 28.4% of patients classified as stage D and 56.4% of patients classified as stage E were reclassified, with lower mortality among those reclassified to less-severe stages. Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest functioned best as a stage modifier, whereas in-hospital cardiac arrest corresponded to stage E. Findings were consistent across HF-CS and MI-CS. The 2026 CS staging system was evaluated in 1,417,637 patients in a geographically and structurally diverse health care system and demonstrated a graded, monotonic increase in mortality across stages A-E.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Using fewer clinical variables, the 2026 CSWG criteria provide a simple framework for CS severity staging that is applicable among patients with HF-CS and MI-CS and can be standardized across clinical trials and health care settings.

articles.conclusion: Using fewer clinical variables, the 2026 CSWG criteria provide a simple framework for CS severity staging that is applicable among patients with HF-CS and MI-CS and can be standardized across clinical trials and health care settings.

articles.title: Prevalence of Transthyretin Amyloidosis Among Older Taiwanese Patients With Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction: The PATCH-HFpEF Study

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a heterogeneous clinical syndrome in which transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CM) has emerged as an important but frequently under-recognized cause, particularly in older patients. Prior studies have suggested that left ventricular (LV) wall thickness ≥12 mm in HFpEF warrants further evaluation; however, whether this applies to Asian patients with smaller body size remains uncertain.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: The authors sought to determine the prevalence of ATTR-CM and identify clinical predictors in older Asian patients with HFpEF.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this prospective multicenter study, patients aged ≥60 years with HFpEF underwent evaluation including echocardiography, laboratory tests, and technetium-99m pyrophosphate scintigraphy. ATTR-CM was diagnosed by multidisciplinary discussion integrating clinical presentation, laboratory evaluation, and multimodality imaging.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 205 patients, 4.4% (9/205; 95% CI: 2.0%-8.2%) were diagnosed with ATTR-CM, all with wild-type. The prevalence of ATTR-CM increased to 10.2% (9/88; 95% CI: 4.8%-18.7%) among patients with LV posterior wall thickness ≥12 mm, whereas no patient with LV wall thickness <12 mm had ATTR-CM. Higher visual score on technetium-99m pyrophosphate scintigraphy was more common with advancing age. In multivariable logistic regression, LV posterior wall thickness (OR: 2.50 per 1 mm increase; 95% CI: 1.54-4.06) and troponin T (OR: 1.15 per 10 ng/L increase; 95% CI: 1.01-1.31) were independently associated with ATTR-CM.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: ATTR-CM is a clinically relevant contributor to HFpEF in older Asian patients, with prevalence markedly enriched among those with increased LV wall thickness. Age, LV wall thickness, and troponin T may facilitate targeted screening and improve recognition of ATTR-CM in older patients with HFpEF.

articles.conclusion: ATTR-CM is a clinically relevant contributor to HFpEF in older Asian patients, with prevalence markedly enriched among those with increased LV wall thickness. Age, LV wall thickness, and troponin T may facilitate targeted screening and improve recognition of ATTR-CM in older patients with HFpEF.

articles.title: Concomitant Transcatheter Aortic and Tricuspid Valve Replacement

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is associated with adverse outcomes.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: A 65-year-old man with advanced right heart failure symptoms and torrential TR was accepted for transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR). After an unforeseen treatment delay, reassessment demonstrated progression of concomitant mild-to-moderate aortic stenosis (AS) to severe AS. He underwent successful TAVR and TTVR during 1 procedure with an excellent clinical outcome.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Given the sequence of disease progression with symptomatic torrential TR preceding the development of severe AS, an indication for TAVR and TTVR was established. A single-procedure strategy was favored over a staged approach based on the assumption that TAVR alone could increase forward flow and right-sided loading conditions, potentially worsening right heart failure.

abstract.label: TAKE-HOME MESSAGES
abstract.text: Concomitant TAVR and TTVR may benefit selected patients. Pre-TAVR identification of patients requiring adjunctive TTVR and determination of the optimal timing (concomitant or staged) remain challenging.

articles.title: Prognostic Impact of Discharge Transprosthetic Tricuspid Gradient After Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Replacement: The TRIPLACE Registry

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Although transprosthetic gradients are established prognostic markers after left-sided valve interventions, the prognostic significance of discharge tricuspid gradient (dTVG) after transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR) remains unclear.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: This study sought to evaluate the association between dTVG and clinical outcomes after TTVR and identify high dTVG determinants.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: TRIPLACE (Global Multicenter Registry on Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Replacement) is an international, multicenter TTVR registry. A discharge landmark analysis was performed, excluding patients with in-hospital mortality, lack of TTVR technical success, missing dTVG, or unavailable follow-up at any time point. Endpoints included all-cause mortality and the composite of all-cause mortality or heart failure hospitalization. The optimal dTVG cutoff was identified through quartile-based survival analysis and confirmed by log-rank maximization. Multivariable Cox models were developed using cross-validated candidate variable selection.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 526 patients, 474 were included. Median follow-up was 208.5 days (Q1-Q3: 54-474 days). A data-driven dTVG cutoff of 3.5 mm Hg identified 122 of 474 patients (25.7%) with high dTVG. dTVG ≥3.5 mm Hg was associated with higher 1- and 3-year mortality (HR: 2.07; 95% CI: 1.14-3.75; P = 0.017 and HR: 2.07; 95% CI: 1.24-3.48; P = 0.006, respectively) and composite endpoint events (HR: 1.99; 95% CI: 1.31-3.03; P = 0.001 and HR: 1.96; 95% CI: 1.33-2.88; P < 0.001). After multivariable adjustment, dTVG ≥3.5 mm Hg remained associated with 3-year mortality (adjusted HR: 1.84; 95% CI: 1.09-3.10; P = 0.022) and the composite endpoint at 1 and 3 years (adjusted HR: 1.77; 95% CI: 1.16-2.70; P = 0.009 and adjusted HR: 1.77; 95% CI: 1.20-2.60; P = 0.004, respectively). Indexed inner transcatheter tricuspid valve diameter was the only potentially modifiable independent predictor of high dTVG (OR: 0.79 per 1 mm/m2 increase; 95% CI: 0.71-0.88).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Elevated dTVG after TTVR independently identifies patients at increased risk of adverse outcomes. A 3.5 mm Hg threshold may support postprocedural risk stratification, whereas inner valve diameter represents a potentially modifiable determinant of elevated dTVG. (TRIPLACE [Global Multicenter Registry on Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Replacement]; NCT06033274).

articles.conclusion: Elevated dTVG after TTVR independently identifies patients at increased risk of adverse outcomes. A 3.5 mm Hg threshold may support postprocedural risk stratification, whereas inner valve diameter represents a potentially modifiable determinant of elevated dTVG. (TRIPLACE [Global Multicenter Registry on Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Replacement]; NCT06033274).

articles.title: Utility of Donor-Recipient HLA Matching in Heart Transplantation in the Era of Extended Donor Organ Preservation: A Multi-Institutional Analysis
articles.journal: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Closer human leukocyte antigen (HLA) match between the donor and the recipient leads to better outcomes after kidney transplantation. Since extended donor preservation is now possible in heart transplantation (HT), we examined the possible impact of prioritization of HLA matching in HT.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We included single organ HT recipients reported to the Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network (OPTN) transplanted in 2010-2019. Outcomes included survival, treated rejection and development of cardiac allograft vasculopathy (CAV) across 5 and 10 year follow-up after transplant. We examined associations between matches at A, B, DR, DPB, DQA, DQB and DPA loci and the outcomes in univariable and multivariable analyses.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: There were 5176 patients in the 5Y cohort with a median of 9 (IQR 8; 11) HLA mismatches and 9118 patients in the 10Y cohort with a median of 6 (IQR 5; 7) HLA mismatches. In adjusted analyses, there was no significant association between donor-recipient HLA match and mortality, treated rejection or CAV in the 5Y cohort. In the 10Y cohort, HLA mismatch was a risk factor for mortality (HR 1.06, CI 1; 1.12, p=0.047) and treated rejection (HR 1.13, CI 1.07;1.2, p<0.001) in adults. Among pediatric patients, HLA mismatch conferred a nominally higher risk of mortality (HR 1.14, CI 0.97; 1.34, p=0.121) and treated rejection (HR 1.08, CI 0.96;1.21, p=0.226).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: We show that the current impact of donor-recipient HLA match on post-HT outcomes is relatively small. While novel organ preservation techniques may make HLA matching feasible, our data do not support its adoption into future iterations of the HT allocation system.

articles.conclusion: We show that the current impact of donor-recipient HLA match on post-HT outcomes is relatively small. While novel organ preservation techniques may make HLA matching feasible, our data do not support its adoption into future iterations of the HT allocation system.

articles.title: Hemodynamic Effects of Reducing LV Afterload With Impella or Intra-Aortic Balloon Counterpulsation During Veno-Arterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation in Cardiogenic Shock: HERACLES Trial

abstract.text: Background: Veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) provides organ support in cardiogenic shock but increases left ventricular (LV) afterload, potentially impairing cardiac recovery. LV unloading with an intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) or micro-axial flow pump (mAFP) may mitigate this effect. HERACLES compared their effects on myocardial oxygen supply and demand. Methods: Patients receiving VA-ECMO for cardiogenic shock were randomized to LV unloading with IABP or mAFP, stratified by ischemic/non-ischemic etiology. Distal coronary, aortic and LV pressures and coronary flow (inverse mean transit time, Tmn) were measured with and without unloading. Myocardial oxygen demand was estimated as the area under the LV pressure curve in systole (TTI) x heart rate (HR). The primary endpoint was the change in myocardial oxygen supply-demand ratio calculated as [(Tmn * TTI*HR)off / (Tmn * TTI *HR)unload]. Secondary endpoints included changes in coronary flow [device flow ratio (DFR) =(Tmn)off/ (Tmn)unload], oxygen demand per beat (DTTI), contractility (DdP/dtmax) and filling pressure (DLVEDP). Results: Twenty-four patients were enrolled (age 51 [46-57]; 46% male; 96% SCAI D/E; 38% ischemic). At randomization, lactate was 4.3 mmol/L [IQR 2.5 to 8.4], LV ejection fraction 10% [10 to 17], LVEDP 18 mmHg [14 to 24]. The myocardial oxygen supply-demand ratio improved with IABP but not mAFP (1.48 [1.23 to 2.10] vs 0.97 [0.92 to 1.39]; P=0.036), driven predominantly by differential reduction of TTI. Coronary pressure increased but flow was unchanged with mAFP (DFR 1.00 [0.86 to 1.13]). Coronary flow increased marginally with IABP (DFR 1.16 [1.00 to 1.51]). LV pressures decreased with both devices and contractility with IABP only, with no between-group differences. Thirty-day mortality was similar (38% vs 45%, p=0.84). Conclusions: In VA-ECMO supported SCAI D/E cardiogenic shock, IABP improved myocardial oxygen supply-demand balance, whereas mAFP did not. Further research is needed to determine whether these mechanistic differences translate to clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Role of Interleukin 34 in Pulmonary Vascular Remodeling Associated With Fibrosing Interstitial Lung Disease

abstract.text: Pulmonary hypertension with fibrosing interstitial lung disease is characterized by progressive pulmonary vascular remodeling and poor prognosis. Although inflammation and macrophage activation contribute to vascular remodeling, upstream mediators remain incompletely defined. Interleukin 34 (IL34), a ligand of colony-stimulating factor-1 receptor, regulates macrophage differentiation and recruitment. The objective is to elucidate the role of IL34 in pulmonary vascular remodeling associated with fibrosing interstitial lung disease. We investigated human lung samples, in vitro studies, using a murine model of pulmonary hypertension with fibrosing interstitial lung disease, and smooth muscle cell-specific IL34-deficient mice. IL34 expression was increased in the pulmonary arteries of patients with fibrosing interstitial lung disease with pulmonary vascular remodeling. IL34 was upregulated in pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells in a murine model of pulmonary hypertension with fibrosing interstitial lung disease, promoting osteopontin production in macrophages. Smooth muscle cell-specific IL34 deficiency attenuated right ventricular systolic pressure, right ventricular hypertrophy, vascular remodeling, and perivascular macrophage accumulation in a murine model of pulmonary hypertension with fibrosing interstitial lung disease. Osteopontin from IL34-induced macrophages promoted pulmonary artery smooth muscle cell proliferation. These findings identify smooth muscle cell-derived IL34 as a contributor to pulmonary vascular remodeling associated with fibrosing interstitial lung disease.

articles.title: Adiponectin and Pulmonary Hypertension Risk: Mendelian Randomization and Receptor-Side Genetic Evidence

abstract.text: Circulating adiponectin is generally considered metabolically protective, but higher levels have been associated with adverse outcomes in some cardiovascular diseases and states of high disease burden, a pattern referred to as the adiponectin paradox. This study assessed genetic evidence relating the adiponectin axis to pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) and pulmonary hypertension (PH)-related phenotypes, with consideration of body mass index (BMI) and ADIPOR1/ADIPOR2-related regulation. We integrated publicly available GWAS data for adiponectin, BMI, and PAH/PH with GTEx quantitative trait locus data. The primary two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis used the GCST90293086 adiponectin GWAS as the exposure and the Rhodes/GCST007228 PAH GWAS as the outcome. Supplementary analyses included FinnGen Release 12, BMI-adjusted multivariable MR, receptor-side cis-MR and MRBEE, ADIPOR2 colocalization, local linkage disequilibrium and proxy variant annotation, and lung tissue sQTL analysis. The primary IVW analysis included 21 variants and indicated a nominally significant positive association between genetically predicted adiponectin and PAH risk (OR = 1.452, 95% CI: 1.033-2.042; p = 0.03195). Complementary MR estimates were similar in direction but did not reach statistical significance. In BMI-adjusted multivariable MR using a different FinnGen PH-related outcome, the adiponectin estimate was negative. Because the outcomes differed, this contrast cannot be attributed to BMI adjustment alone. Receptor-side analyses provided supportive genetic evidence involving ADIPOR1/ADIPOR2, including ADIPOR2 colocalization and lung tissue sQTL findings. These exploratory findings do not establish a direct harmful causal effect of circulating adiponectin or confirm a receptor-mediated molecular mechanism.

articles.title: Sex-Specific Mechanisms and Therapeutics in Heart Failure: Translating Biology into Personalized Care

abstract.text: Sex is one of the most consistent, yet clinically underexploited, determinants of heart failure phenotype, mechanism and outcome. Building on landmark reviews and the 2024 scientific statement of the Heart Failure Association, which documented well-recognized phenotypic differences but noted that their mechanisms remain only partially defined, this review examines how sex differences in heart failure arise and how firmly they should guide practice. Epidemiologically, female predominance in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction is age- and menopause-dependent rather than lifelong. Mechanistically, sex-divergent hormonal signalling, autonomic tone, coronary microvascular dysfunction and myocardial fibrosis often produce similar phenotypes through different mechanisms: microvascular dysfunction is similarly prevalent in both sexes but linked to fibrosis in women and to atherosclerotic risk factors in men, and oestradiol regulates collagen synthesis in opposite directions in female and male cardiac fibroblasts. Clinically, comorbidities carry divergent prognostic weight by sex. Graded against the strength of evidence, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors show established sex-neutral efficacy, whereas the greater benefit of angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibition and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonism in women rests on subgroup signals that await confirmation. Natriuretic peptide concentrations are substantially sex-dependent, yet diagnostic thresholds remain sex-neutral, although sex-specific calibration is methodologically achievable. Women remain underrepresented in heart failure trials and less often referred to specialized care. Heart failure is therefore best understood as a sex-differentiated syndrome whose frameworks were built largely around male-pattern disease. Sex-calibrated trial enrolment, sex-specific biomarker and ejection fraction thresholds, and stratification by menopausal stage are concrete next steps towards personalized care.

articles.title: Histologically Confirmed Myxedematous Myocardial Involvement in Severe Hypothyroidism With Concomitant Bicuspid Aortic Stenosis

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Histologically confirmed myxedematous myocardial involvement is rare and may be difficult to recognize when another cause of ventricular hypertrophy and fibrosis coexists.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: A 40-year-old man with longstanding, inadequately treated primary hypothyroidism presented with exertional dyspnea and a large goiter. Echocardiography showed severe bicuspid aortic stenosis, moderate aortic regurgitation, marked concentric left ventricular hypertrophy, preserved ejection fraction, and severely reduced global longitudinal strain. Cardiac magnetic resonance demonstrated extensive late gadolinium enhancement involving approximately 26% of myocardial mass. After thyroid optimization, he underwent aortic valve replacement. Myocardial biopsy showed severe cardiomyocyte atrophy, interstitial mucin deposition, and extensive replacement fibrosis; Congo red staining was negative.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Severe aortic stenosis provided an alternative explanation for the myocardial phenotype, and multimodality imaging alone could not distinguish pressure-overload remodeling from hypothyroidism-related myocardial injury.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Histopathology established concomitant myxedematous myocardial involvement, highlighting the diagnostic value of tissue characterization in severe hypothyroidism.

articles.conclusion: Histopathology established concomitant myxedematous myocardial involvement, highlighting the diagnostic value of tissue characterization in severe hypothyroidism.

articles.title: Impact of Showering Methods on Driveline Exit Site Microbiology and Driveline Infection in Patients With Left Ventricular Assist Devices
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)

abstract.text: Driveline infection (DLI) remains a major complication in patients with a left ventricular assist device (LVAD). This study evaluated the impact of different showering methods on bacterial colonization at the driveline exit site (DLES) and the incidence of DLI. Patients who underwent LVAD implantation at our institute from 2008 to 2021 were included and classified into two groups: the open group, in which the DLES was exposed and washed with running water, and the covered group, in which the DLES was sealed with a waterproof dressing during showering. The primary outcome was the incidence of DLI within 3 years following hospital discharge. A total of 103 patients were included (the open group, n = 47; the covered group, n = 56). The DLI-free rate was significantly higher in the covered group than the open group (77% vs. 49%; p = 0.003). Pseudomonas aeruginosa was detected less frequently at the DLES, and DLI caused by P. aeruginosa was significantly reduced in the covered group. Multivariate analysis suggested that the open showering method was an independent risk factor for DLI (hazard ratio, 2.816; 95% confidence interval, 1.325-5.984; p = 0.007). The covered showering method was associated with a significantly lower incidence of DLI, particularly infections caused by P. aeruginosa.

articles.title: Outcomes and Complications of Axillary Intra-Aortic Balloon Pump Support: A Single-Center Experience
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)

abstract.text: Axillary intra-aortic balloon pump (axi-IABP) support has emerged as an alternative to femoral access for patients with advanced heart failure, offering improved mobility and potential benefits in pretransplant conditioning; however, data on associated complications remain limited. We conducted a retrospective study of 55 patients who underwent axi-IABP placement between January 2019 and July 2025 at our institution. The cohort had a median age of 59 (interquartile range [IQR], 52-65) years and presented with cardiogenic shock requiring mechanical circulatory support (MCS). Axi-IABP successfully bridged 87.3% of patients to advanced therapies. A total of 83 complications were identified in 60.0% of patients, most commonly malposition in 23.6% of patients, gas leak alarms in 16.4% of patients, and kinking in 16.4% of patients. Serious vascular complications were infrequent. The median time to first complication was 10.5 (IQR, 2.75-25.5) days. Female sex was associated with a higher hazard of first complication when controlled for height (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] = 2.75, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.04-7.27; p = 0.041). In conclusion, axi-IABP is an effective bridging strategy that enhances patient mobility but is associated with a high rate of device-related complications, predominantly mechanical in nature, underscoring the importance of careful patient selection and monitoring.

articles.title: Iliohypogastric and Ilioinguinal Nerve Block for Awake ECPella Cannulation in Pediatric Patients With Nonpostcardiotomy Cardiogenic Shock
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)

abstract.text: In pediatric cardiogenic shock, endotracheal intubation may carry a high risk of cardiac arrest during anesthesia induction. This single-center retrospective case series (2020-2025) evaluated the feasibility, safety, and outcomes of ultrasound (US)-guided ilioinguinal-iliohypogastric (IhIG) nerve blocks (0.05-0.1 ml/kg of 0.25% ropivacaine) under light sedation to facilitate awake venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation and Impella (ECPella) surgical cannulation. Five adolescents (median age: 13 years, range: 7-17; median weight: 45 kg, range: 21-58) with nonpostcardiotomy cardiogenic shock underwent successful IhIG block placement in the pediatric intensive care unit by anesthesia-trained intensivists, followed by surgical cannulation in the catheterization laboratory. Intubation and mechanical ventilation were avoided during initial cannulation and throughout ECPella duration. Three patients required a modified chimney Y-graft for cannula placement, and two experienced local surgical bleeding. All five patients survived to hospital discharge, with three achieving direct biventricular recovery. Based on these preliminary data, US-guided IhIG nerve block seems a feasible and safe strategy for awake ECPella cannulation in selected pediatric patients, successfully avoiding high-risk invasive ventilation and general anesthesia.

articles.title: National Use Patterns and Comparative Effectiveness of Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation in Myocardial Infarction-Related Cardiogenic Shock
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) provides bi-ventricular support for patients with myocardial infarction-related cardiogenic shock (MI-CS); comparative effectiveness data relative to other mechanical circulatory support remain limited. We characterize contemporary ECMO utilization for MI-CS and compare short-term mortality across ECMO and non-ECMO treatment strategies.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We compared baseline characteristics and temporal trends in mechanical circulatory support utilization among Medicare beneficiaries hospitalized with MI-CS from 2016 to 2023 and treated with ECMO, Impella, intra-aortic balloon pump, or medical management alone. Patient outcomes for each group were evaluated using inverse probability of treatment weighting, G-formula approach, and grace period analysis. The primary endpoint was 30-day all-cause mortality.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The cohort included 102 718 patients: 1165 (1.1%) treated with ECMO, 10 064 (9.8%) Impella, 24 631 (24.0%) intra-aortic balloon pump, and 66 858 (65.1%) medical management alone. From 2016 to 2023, ECMO use for MI-CS increased from 0.8% to 1.8%. The percentage of hospitals using ECMO increased from 9.2% to 17.1%. Unadjusted 30-day mortality was higher for ECMO (69%) compared with Impella (60%), intra-aortic balloon pump (39%), and medical management (46%) (all P<0.0001). Adjusted inverse probability of treatment weighting and G-formula analyses revealed a 30-day mortality rate of 68%-70% for ECMO, which was higher than that for other therapies. The grace period analysis revealed similar mortality between patients treated with ECMO (54%) and Impella (54%).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: ECMO use in a contemporary Medicare cohort of patients with MI-CS was infrequent (1.1%) and associated with high 30-day mortality. Despite use of complementary causal inference methods, we were unable to establish valid causal inferences on ECMO use and patient survival.

articles.conclusion: ECMO use in a contemporary Medicare cohort of patients with MI-CS was infrequent (1.1%) and associated with high 30-day mortality. Despite use of complementary causal inference methods, we were unable to establish valid causal inferences on ECMO use and patient survival.

articles.title: Integrated Network Pharmacology and Experimental Validation Implicate AKT1-Associated Signaling in the Protective Effects of Panax notoginseng Against Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension

abstract.text: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a progressive and fatal cardiopulmonary disease characterized by pulmonary vascular remodeling, endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, and increased pulmonary vascular resistance. Despite advances in targeted therapies, effective treatment options remain limited. This study investigated the molecular mechanisms underlying the therapeutic effects of Panax notoginseng against PAH through integrated computational and experimental validation. Network pharmacology was employed to identify the bioactive compounds and therapeutic targets of Panax notoginseng. Functional enrichment, protein-protein interaction network analysis, transcriptomic validation, molecular docking, surface plasmon resonance (SPR), molecular dynamics simulation, and MM/PBSA analyses were performed to characterize representative target-compound interactions. Experimental validation to predict the therapeutic mechanism was performed using RAW264.7 macrophages, pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells (PASMCs), and a Sugen5416/hypoxia-induced murine model of PAH. A total of 67 overlapping therapeutic targets were identified, with enrichment analyses highlighting inflammation, oxidative stress, apoptosis, vascular remodeling, and the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway. AKT1 was identified as a central hub gene and was significantly upregulated under hypoxic conditions. Quercetin and Liquiritigenin (DFV)exhibited stable interactions with AKT1, with quercetin demonstrating stronger binding affinity (-11.10 kcal/mol) than liquiritigenin (-9.33 kcal/mol). Consistent with these computational predictions, Panax notoginseng reduced AKT1 expression and phosphorylation, attenuated oxidative stress and inflammatory cytokine production, inhibited PASMC proliferation and migration, and significantly improved pulmonary hemodynamics, right ventricular hypertrophy, and pulmonary vascular remodeling in vivo. Collectively, these findings identify AKT1 as a key molecular target through which Panax notoginseng exerts therapeutic effects against PAH in vivo.

articles.title: Pulmonary Endarterectomy After Balloon Pulmonary Angioplasty: A Single-Center USA Experience

abstract.text: Pulmonary endarterectomy (PEA) is the treatment of choice for operable chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH), while balloon pulmonary angioplasty (BPA) is reserved for inoperable disease. However, operability is subjective and there are patients who may undergo BPA prior to PEA. It is not clear if prior BPA affects PEA outcomes. We present a series of patients from a single, high-volume, referral center who underwent PEA after prior BPA. CTEPH patients who underwent BPA prior to undergoing PEA at the University of California, San Diego between January 2013 and July 2025 were included. Post-PEA outcomes were compared to all PEA patients who did not have prior BPA from the year 2022. Twenty-one patients were identified. Average number of BPA sessions prior to PEA was 3.4 ± 2.1. The most common reason for initial BPA was distal disease deemed inoperable (43%). Average total circulatory arrest time was 61.5 ± 21.8 min, compared to 47.9 ± 19.3 min (p = 0.003) in the control PEA cases (n = 188). Post-operatively, the PEA after BPA cohort had longer ventilator days (p < 0.001), ICU days (p = 0.022) and post-operative length of stay (LOS) (p < 0.001); there were also higher rates of post-operative bleeding (p < 0.001) requiring transfusions (p = 0.033) and return to the operating room (p = 0.008). There was one death related to prior BPA complications despite adequate endarterectomy with improved hemodynamics. There was similar hemodynamic improvement post-operatively in both cohorts. Although prior BPA made PEA more challenging and increased select post-operative complications, it is not a contraindication for successful PEA.

articles.title: Evaluation of an Echocardiography-Based Artificial Intelligence Algorithm for Early HFpEF Detection: A HeartShare/AMP-HF Cohort Study

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Early heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is difficult to identify because of nonspecific symptoms and subtle echocardiographic abnormalities. EchoGo HF, an FDA-cleared artificial intelligence (AI) model, estimates HFpEF probability from a single apical 4-chamber echocardiographic clip, but has been validated only in patients with clinically adjudicated HFpEF.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: This study aims to evaluate whether AI-HFpEF can detect early HFpEF in community-dwelling adults without a clinical heart failure (HF) diagnosis and predict incident clinical HFpEF in patients within a health system.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The authors included 2 community cohorts (the MESA [Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis] Early HF study and the DHMS [Dallas Hearts and Minds Study]). Early HFpEF was defined by impaired exercise capacity or health-related quality of life with objective evidence of elevated cardiac filling pressures in patients without clinically diagnosed HF. The AI-HFpEF model was applied to resting echocardiograms, and the diagnostic performance was assessed. Multivariable models examined associations between AI-HFpEF output and early HFpEF phenotype. Separately, we included adults in the UTSW (University of Texas Southwestern) Health System with structurally normal echocardiograms and no prior HF (2018-2024) and assessed the association of AI-HFpEF output with incident HFpEF (adjudicated using a validated registry) using Cox regression.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In MESA (N = 2,544; 8.3% early HFpEF), AI-HFpEF outperformed H2FPEF for detecting early HFpEF (area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve [AUROC]: 0.77 vs 0.70). AI-HFpEF diagnostic positivity was associated with higher odds of early HFpEF (OR: 3.26; P < 0.001), lower 6-minute walk distance, and lower Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-12-Clinical Summary Score. Similarly, in DHMS (N = 624; 18.6% early HFpEF), AI-HFpEF outperformed H2FPEF (AUROC: 0.83 vs 0.77), and diagnostic positivity was associated with early HFpEF (OR: 6.76; P < 0.001), shorter exercise duration, and lower peak oxygen uptake. In the UTSW cohort (N = 6,876; median follow-up = 33 months; incident HFpEF = 3.4%), an AI-HFpEF diagnostic positive result was associated with >2-fold higher incident HFpEF risk (aHR: 2.08; P < 0.001). This association persisted across all conventional diastolic dysfunction grades.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: AI-HFpEF identified the early HFpEF phenotype in community-dwelling adults and independently predicted incident clinical HFpEF among patients in a health system.

articles.conclusion: AI-HFpEF identified the early HFpEF phenotype in community-dwelling adults and independently predicted incident clinical HFpEF among patients in a health system.

articles.title: Exercise chronotropic inefficiency in patients with heart failure across distinct left ventricular ejection fraction phenotypes

abstract.label: AIMS
abstract.text: To characterize the pattern of chronotropic incompetence (CI) response to exercise in patients with heart failure (HF) across distinct phenotypes of the left ventricular ejection fraction and to explore the extent to which heart rate (HR) response should be prioritized as a therapeutic target within personalized HF management strategies.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Patients with HF with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), and healthy controls underwent incremental exercise testing with simultaneous gas exchange and echocardiography assessments. Stroke volume (SV), HR, cardiac output (CO), and arteriovenous oxygen difference [C(a-v)O2] were assessed from rest to peak exercise. Graphical analyses explored relationships amongst determinants of oxygen uptake (V̇O2).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Both HF phenotypes exhibited CI and a blunted increase in CO during exercise compared with controls. Peak HR was similarly reduced by 20% in HFpEF and 23% in HFrEF. HFpEF, however, exhibited a steeper HR-VO2 relationship. HFrEF demonstrated a greater compensatory increase in peripheral O2 extraction, with peak C(a-v)O2 73% higher than controls and 21% higher than HFpEF. In contrast, HFpEF showed limited ability to augment C(a-v)O2 and presented the lowest relative peak V̇O2 (-39% vs. controls and -16% vs. HFrEF), despite similar peak V̇O2%pred between HF phenotypes.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: CI can contribute to exercise intolerance in both HF phenotypes, with distinct compensatory mechanisms. An integrated cardiopulmonary exercise testing-echocardiography approach may support identifying phenotype-specific physiological profiles that might address therapeutic strategies targeting CI, SV reserve, and peripheral O2 utilization to improve functional capacity in HF. Addressing the kinetics of HR slope and ΔHR metrics seems relevant to implement knowledge on the fundamental CI contribution in HF phenotypes.

articles.conclusion: CI can contribute to exercise intolerance in both HF phenotypes, with distinct compensatory mechanisms. An integrated cardiopulmonary exercise testing-echocardiography approach may support identifying phenotype-specific physiological profiles that might address therapeutic strategies targeting CI, SV reserve, and peripheral O2 utilization to improve functional capacity in HF. Addressing the kinetics of HR slope and ΔHR metrics seems relevant to implement knowledge on the fundamental CI contribution in HF phenotypes.

articles.title: Electrical Storm in Advanced Chagas Cardiomyopathy Treated With Stereotactic Arrhythmia Radiotherapy After LVAD Implantation

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Refractory ventricular tachycardia (VT) in advanced Chagas cardiomyopathy remains challenging after prior ablation and mechanical circulatory support.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: A 40-year-old man with advanced Chagas cardiomyopathy and prior endo-epicardial VT ablation developed electrical storm during influenza A infection and underwent left ventricular assist device implantation as a bridge to transplantation. Despite unloading, antiarrhythmic therapy, overdrive pacing, and stellate ganglion modulation, monomorphic VT persisted. Repeat ablation was unfavorable because of frailty and extensive residual lateral scar. Targeting for stereotactic arrhythmia radiotherapy (STAR) integrated late gadolinium enhancement cardiac magnetic resonance, clinical VT morphology, prior electroanatomic mapping, and planning computed tomography. A single 25-Gy fraction was delivered without acute complications. No sustained VT or implantable cardioverter-defibrillator shocks occurred during follow-up.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Multimodality-guided STAR was feasible in this critically ill left ventricular assist device-supported patient. Although stabilization cannot be attributed to STAR alone, radiotherapy was delivered without observed acute radiotherapy- or device-related complications.

abstract.label: TAKE-HOME MESSAGE
abstract.text: STAR may offer a noninvasive substrate-targeted option when repeat ablation is limited.

articles.title: Early Diagnosis, Delayed Treatment, and Fulminant Progression of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor-Associated Myocarditis

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Prompt immunosuppressive therapy is recommended for immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis; however, the optimal timing in asymptomatic patients remains uncertain.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: A woman in her 60s receiving adjuvant pembrolizumab for melanoma developed asymptomatic cardiac troponin I (cTnI) elevation (93 pg/mL) before her ninth cycle. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging met diagnostic criteria for myocarditis; however, immunosuppressive therapy was withheld because of the absence of symptoms and mild cTnI elevation. One week later, she developed symptomatic myocarditis with a marked cTnI increase (4,115 pg/mL), requiring intensive care, corticosteroid pulse therapy, and temporary mechanical circulatory support.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: This case demonstrates that asymptomatic immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis can progress rapidly despite seemingly low initial risk, underscoring the importance of ongoing risk assessment following diagnosis.

abstract.label: TAKE-HOME MESSAGES
abstract.text: Early diagnosis alone may not be sufficient to prevent disease progression. Risk stratification and timely intervention during the presymptomatic phase may improve patient outcomes.

articles.title: Diuretics for Management of Bronchopulmonary Dysplasia Associated Pulmonary Hypertension in Preterm Infants-A Systematic Review

abstract.text: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia associated pulmonary hypertension (BPD-PH) in preterm infants results from impaired pulmonary vascular development and contributes significantly to morbidity and mortality. Diuretics are commonly used to reduce pulmonary vascular congestion and improve oxygenation, but their efficacy and safety remain unclear. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of diuretic use in preterm infants with BPD-PH. Primary outcomes were mortality and need for home respiratory support; secondary outcomes were echocardiographic and clinical parameters, and adverse effects such as hyponatremia, nephrocalcinosis. We searched MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Central, and ClinicalTrials.gov from inception to October 2025. We included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and non-randomized studies of interventions (NRSI) evaluating diuretics in preterm infants (< 32 weeks' gestation) with BPD-PH diagnosed by echocardiography at 36 weeks postmenstrual age. Two reviewers independently performed data extraction and risk-of-bias assessment (ROBINS-I). Outcomes were synthesized narratively, and a meta-analysis was performed where sufficient data were available. Of 492 studies identified, 2 NRSI (n = 49) met inclusion criteria, both were at serious risk of bias. No RCTs exist on diuretics for BPD-PH in preterm infants. Mortality, respiratory, discharge outcomes and adverse effects were reported inconsistently. Meta-analysis of limited data demonstrated small improvements in echocardiographic markers, but the certainty of evidence was very low due to heterogeneity between the two included studies. To conclude, evidence supporting the use of diuretics in BPD-PH in preterm infants remains limited and of low certainty. High quality studies are needed to better define their safety and efficacy.

articles.title: Procedural Volume and Outcomes After Balloon Pulmonary Angioplasty for Chronic Thromboembolic Pulmonary Hypertension

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Balloon pulmonary angioplasty (BPA) is an established treatment for inoperable chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension; however, volume-outcome relationships remain unclear.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: This study examined the relationship between hospital and operator volume and BPA-related complications using a nationwide registry.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The authors analyzed 5,403 BPA sessions for chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension in the Japanese Structural Heart Diseases registry between 2021 and 2024. Procedural volume was defined as BPA sessions performed during the preceding 3 years. The primary outcome was a composite of BPA-related complications. Mixed-effects logistic regression models accounted for hospital and operator clustering.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: BPA-related complications occurred in 751 sessions (13.9%). Severe complications were uncommon, with 3 periprocedural deaths, 6 requiring invasive mechanical ventilation, and 7 requiring extracorporeal membrane oxygenation. The main categorical analysis revealed that hospital BPA volume ≥150 sessions/3 years was associated with higher odds of BPA-related complications (adjusted OR: 1.60; 95% CI: 1.08-2.36; P = 0.019), whereas operator volume was not independently associated. When hospital and operator volumes were modeled separately as continuous variables, each was associated with complications. However, neither remained independently associated after mutual adjustment. In an analysis restricted to 135 complications considered less susceptible to differences in ascertainment, no statistically significant association was detected for either volume measure, although the smaller number of events limited statistical precision.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: BPA-related complications demonstrated a complex relationship with procedural volume, while severe complications remained uncommon. articles.title: The clinical chameleon: eosinophilic myocarditis presenting as acute coronary syndrome-a case report

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Eosinophilic myocarditis is a rare inflammatory cardiomyopathy that may clinically mimic acute coronary syndrome and should be considered in patients with non-obstructive coronary arteries, often resulting in diagnostic delay.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: A 27-year-old man presented with recurrent chest pain and was initially misdiagnosed with a panic attack. On admission, laboratory evaluation revealed marked peripheral eosinophilia (1800/mm3), mildly elevated troponin, and increased serum IgE levels. Echocardiography demonstrated reduced left ventricular ejection fraction and a large apical intracavitary thrombus. Coronary angiography revealed normal coronary arteries. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging showed myocardial oedema and circumferential subendocardial late gadolinium enhancement consistent with eosinophilic myocarditis. Extensive aetiological workup was negative. Although endomyocardial biopsy showed non-specific findings, the diagnosis was established through multimodal integration of clinical, imaging, and laboratory data. High-dose corticosteroid therapy and anticoagulation resulted in rapid clinical improvement, recovery of ventricular function, and near-complete thrombus resolution.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Eosinophilic myocarditis should be considered in young patients presenting with chest pain and non-obstructive coronary arteries. Multimodality imaging-particularly cardiac magnetic resonance-plays a key role in diagnosis, while early corticosteroid therapy may lead to rapid clinical and functional recovery.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: This case underscores the importance of maintaining a high index of clinical suspicion for EM in young patients presenting with chest pain and peripheral eosinophilia. A multimodal diagnostic approach integrating cMRI findings, laboratory data, and exclusion of alternative aetiologies is essential when biopsy results are inconclusive. Early immunosuppressive therapy is key to reversing myocardial damage and preventing progression to end-stage heart failure.

articles.title: Norepinephrine Equivalent Dose for Mortality Risk Stratification in VA-ECMO Cardiogenic Shock

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Patients with cardiogenic shock (CS) complicated by vasoplegia requiring venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) often need escalating vasopressor support and face high mortality. Norepinephrine equivalent dose (NEE) quantifies vasopressor burden, yet its prognostic value in VA-ECMO remains undefined.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: We aimed to characterize the dose-response relationship between NEE and 30-day mortality, identify a clinically relevant NEE threshold, and determine factors associated with high vasopressor burden.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This bicentric retrospective study included 572 consecutive patients with CS requiring VA-ECMO. We collected vasopressor regimens, NEE trajectories, and hemodynamic parameters at predefined intervals. Restricted cubic splines assessed dose-response linearity. Maximally selected rank statistics with bootstrap validation identified optimal thresholds. Cox models estimated mortality risk. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with high vasopressor burden.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The median NEE at ECMO initiation was 0.30 (IQR: 0.09-0.72) μg·kg-1·min-1; 86.2% received norepinephrine. NEE showed a linear dose-response with mortality (HR: 1.06 per 0.1 μg·kg-1·min-1 increment; 95% CI: 1.04-1.08; P < 0.001). A threshold of 0.443 μg·kg-1·min-1 identified high vasopressor burden with elevated 30-day mortality (61.8% vs 42.6%; P < 0.001; adjusted HR: 1.42; 95% CI: 1.11-1.81; P = 0.005). Factors associated with high vasopressor burden included mechanical ventilation (OR: 2.96; 95% CI: 1.08-8.07), prior epinephrine use (OR: 1.87; 95% CI: 1.12-3.14), renal replacement therapy before VA-ECMO (OR: 1.76; 95% CI: 1.02-3.03), baseline lactate (OR: 1.05 per mmol/L; 95% CI: 1.01-1.09), and lower Survival After Veno-Arterial ECMO score (OR: 0.96 per point; 95% CI: 0.92-1.00). Left ventricular unloading was inversely associated (OR: 0.54; 95% CI: 0.34-0.87).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In VA-ECMO-supported CS with vasoplegia, vasopressor burden shows a linear relationship with mortality. A NEE threshold of 0.443 μg·kg-1·min-1 may identify patients with elevated mortality risk.

articles.conclusion: In VA-ECMO-supported CS with vasoplegia, vasopressor burden shows a linear relationship with mortality. A NEE threshold of 0.443 μg·kg-1·min-1 may identify patients with elevated mortality risk.

articles.title: Multi-modal AI: Integrating electrocardiography with molecular biomarkers for noninvasive detection of cardiac allograft rejection

abstract.label: UNLABELLED
abstract.text: Noninvasive rejection biomarkers (AlloMap, AlloSure) demonstrate high negative predictive value but positive predictive values of only 10-30%, driving avoidable endomyocardial biopsies. We developed a multi-modal AI model integrating electrocardiography with molecular biomarkers in 389 heart transplant recipients (5338 ECG-biopsy pairs), performing the first head-to-head comparison of AI-ECG, AlloMap, AlloSure, and their integration against biopsy-proven rejection. Individual modalities showed modest discrimination (AI-ECG AUC 0.65; AlloSure 0.67; AlloMap 0.56), while combining biomarkers alone did not improve performance (AUC 0.65). In the multi-modal test subset of ECGs (n=38, 2 rejection events), the integrated model achieved AUC 0.81 with 100% specificity (0/36 false positives) and 97% negative predictive value, eliminating all 19 false-positive combined-biomarker referrals. These hypothesis-generating results support prospective multi-center validation to determine whether requiring concordance across electrical and biomarker signals reduces unnecessary biopsies while preserving high negative predictive value.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Noninvasive rejection biomarkers (AlloMap gene-expression profiling (GEP); AlloSure donor-derived cell-free DNA (dd-cfDNA)) deliver high negative predictive value but positive predictive values of only 10-30%, driving avoidable endomyocardial biopsies. Each biomarker interrogates a single biological compartment. Whether integrating AI-enabled electrocardiography (AI-ECG) with these molecular assays improves specificity has not been tested.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We retrospectively assembled 5338 unique ECG-endomyocardial-biopsy pairs from 389 adult heart transplant recipients at a single center (2018-2024). A ResNet-18 convolutional neural network was trained on 8-lead ECG waveforms with clinical covariates. In the 340-patient subset with same encounter AlloMap and AlloSure testing (405 ECG-biomarker-biopsy triplets), an integrated model fused the ECG embedding with biomarker values via late concatenation. We performed the first head-to-head, same-cohort comparison of AI-ECG, AlloMap, AlloSure, and their integration against biopsy-proven rejection (ISHLT ≥2R ACR or pAMR ≥2). Discrimination was evaluated with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Individual modalities showed modest discrimination (AI-ECG AUC 0.65, 95% CI 0.58-0.72; AlloSure 0.67, 0.56-0.78; AlloMap 0.56, 0.46-0.67); combining biomarkers alone did not improve performance (AUC 0.65). In the multi-modal test subset (n=38 ECG-biopsy pairs, 2 rejection events), the integrated model achieved AUC 0.81 (0.50-1.00), 100% specificity (36/36; Clopper-Pearson 90-100%), and 97% NPV. At the same NPV threshold, all 19 false-positive combined-biomarker referrals in this subset would have been avoided, though this estimate reflects a single operating point in a small sample. AUC gains over single modalities did not reach statistical significance (DeLong p=0.31-0.34) given the limited event count.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: A multi-modal AI model that requires concordance across electrical, immune-transcriptional, and donor-DNA signals showed numerically higher specificity for cardiac allograft rejection than any single modality, although the corresponding AUC differences did not reach statistical significance. These hypothesis-generating findings suggest that cross-compartment concordance may help discriminate true rejection from biomarker noise, but the small multi-modal test set precludes definitive conclusions; a pre-specified prospective multi-center trial powered for ≥50 rejection events is the necessary next step to test this hypothesis.
